Study-Disjoint Train/Validation Split

Source: R/study_tools.R
stabl_multiomic_study_split.Rd

Assigns whole studies to a training and a validation split so that stabl_multiomic_train_validate() evaluates a cross-study deployment setting rather than a sample-i.i.d. one. Studies are assigned largest-first by a deterministic greedy pass targeting prop_train of the samples while keeping outcome class proportions as balanced as possible across the two sides; a seeded shuffle fixes the order of size ties.

Usage

stabl_multiomic_study_split(
  x_list,
  y,
  study_labels,
  prop_train = 0.75,
  stratified = TRUE,
  random_state = NULL
)

Arguments

x_list

Named list of omic matrices or data frames with identical sample row names.

y

Named outcome vector aligned to x_list rows.

study_labels

Named vector assigning each sample to a study; names must cover exactly the sample IDs. Each study must contain at least 2 samples, and at least 2 studies are required.

prop_train

Target proportion of samples in the training split (strictly between 0 and 1).

stratified

Logical. When TRUE (default), class-proportion imbalance is the secondary assignment criterion after the size target.

random_state

Optional integer seed for deterministic splits.

Value

A list with train_ids, valid_ids (sample IDs in the original row order), study_assignment (named vector mapping each study to "train" or "valid"), class_counts (per-side held-out outcome counts), and fold_scheme = "study_disjoint".

Details

prop_train is a target, not a guarantee: study granularity governs the achievable split, and extreme values can fail the fail-closed checks below.

For a continuous y the balance criterion is computed on factor(as.character(y)) — every distinct value becomes its own class — so the stratification term is degenerate; supply a categorical y (or bin a continuous one) for the balance criterion to be meaningful (review A11).

Examples

set.seed(6L)
ids <- paste0("s", 1:12)
y <- setNames(factor(rep(c("A", "B"), times = 6L)), ids)
x <- matrix(rnorm(12 * 4), 12, 4, dimnames = list(ids, paste0("g", 1:4)))
study_labels <- setNames(rep(paste0("study", 1:3), each = 4L), ids)
split <- stabl_multiomic_study_split(
  x_list = list(rna = x), y = y, study_labels = study_labels,
  prop_train = 2 / 3, random_state = 6L
)
split$study_assignment
#>  study1  study2  study3 
#> "valid" "train" "train"
